title: Integrate security into the SDLC
question: Place security activities and decision gates across an SDLC and explain how methodology affects timing, ownership, and evidence.
scenario: A sprint adds a payment API and changes authorization logic.
focalRelation: Refine security requirements, threat-model the changed flow, review authorization and secrets handling, run automated and targeted abuse tests, verify telemetry, and retain evidence before release.

prediction.prompt: A sprint adds a payment API and changes authorization logic. Which security work belongs in this increment?

options.label: Rely on the annual penetration test because it evaluates the integrated system.
options.feedback: The annual test arrives after this decision and may not exercise the changed object/action flow or release criteria.

options.label: Accept the change because the approved Agile framework already includes security responsibilities.
options.feedback: A delivery framework does not supply the change-specific requirement, threat decision, review, test, or operational evidence.

options.label: Update requirements and threat model, review enforcement and secrets, run abuse tests, and verify telemetry before release.
options.feedback: Correct. The changed flow receives timely design, implementation, negative-test, and operational evidence.

prediction.hint: Identify what changed in the flow and the earliest evidence that can challenge it.

transfer.prompt: A team says an approved agile framework removes the need for threat modeling.

options.label: Add lightweight threat modeling and abuse-case acceptance to the increment workflow
options.feedback: Correct. Add lightweight threat modeling and abuse-case acceptance to the increment workflow.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: A team says an approved agile framework removes the need for threat modeling. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Refine security requirements, threat-model the changed flow, review authorization and secrets handling, run automated and targeted abuse tests, verify telemetry, and retain evidence before release. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Add lightweight threat modeling and abuse-case acceptance to the increment workflow.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: A team says an approved agile framework removes the need for threat modeling. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Refine security requirements, threat-model the changed flow, review authorization and secrets handling, run automated and targeted abuse tests, verify telemetry, and retain evidence before release. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A sprint adds a public webhook after the increment’s threat review and acceptance criteria were approved. What should happen before release?

options.label: Release it and defer security review to the next quarterly architecture cycle
options.feedback: The webhook creates a current release boundary and needs current acceptance evidence.

options.label: Update the threat model and abuse cases, revise acceptance criteria, and test the webhook within the increment
options.feedback: Correct. Agile change does not freeze security assumptions made before a new exposure path.

options.label: Assume the web framework secures the webhook because the rest of the application passed
options.feedback: Framework controls do not establish this endpoint’s authentication, authorization, replay, input, and abuse behavior.

retry.hint: The new trust boundary changes the increment’s threat and test assumptions.

takeaway: Refine security requirements, threat-model the changed flow, review authorization and secrets handling, run automated and targeted abuse tests, verify telemetry, and retain evidence before release.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Security work belongs in each increment that changes risk, requirements, architecture, code, or operation. Early threat modeling and abuse tests complement rather than replace runtime monitoring, patching, incident response, and retirement.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A lifecycle view could place security activities, owners, gates, evidence, and operational feedback at the stages they affect; the opening change/requirement pair cannot.
